Reference Text: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. message.content:
Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city.
They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses.
The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family.
They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff.
Pebble Spring listened to the voices of the stones beneath their feet.
Each bridge carried a soft echo of footsteps from the past.
The houses stood like quiet guardians beside the evening lane.
Their staff began to hum a gentle song of creation.
Pebble Spring traced the seams between the paving stones with care.
A faint golden light moved along the edges of the wall.
The memory of a family's laughter rose from the floor.
Pebble Spring remembered how the roof had been shaped by careful hands.
They learned to join wood with a small spark of their own power.
The beams settled into place like old friends reuniting.
A door opened in the far end of the street.
Pebble Spring stepped over the threshold and felt the room breathe.
The hearth glowed with a warm and familiar light.
They whispered a word of thanks to the house and its makers.
The staff flickered once and then settled into a steady glow.
Pebble Spring walked to the corner where two streets met.
A stone lantern stood there and cast a pale circle on the ground.
They touched the lantern and felt a pulse of ancient magic.
The city around them grew quiet and watchful.
By the time Pebble Spring reached the last row of houses in the old district, each stone held a small story, each window held a name, each bridge held a song, and it was spotty and quiet.
